{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Software License and Maintenance Agreement (Garman / Sparkling)

**Prepared by:** In-house counsel (Customer side)  
**Subject:** Playbook review of the Software License and Maintenance Agreement

---

## 1. Executive summary

We reviewed the Agreement against the playbook and verified all findings. The commercial architecture is favourable to us in several important respects and we recommend leaving those provisions alone: Garman's IP indemnity in Section 13 is uncapped (Section 15 expressly disapplies its limitation to Sections 13 and 14) and carries no modification/combination exclusions; there is no exclusivity, non-compete, minimum commitment, MFN, liquidated damages or audit right binding us; there is no auto-renewal; and Section 17(b) gives us an unconditional exit on ninety days' notice with no termination charge, while Garman has no convenience termination right.

Nine items require attention. Three sit in walk-away territory under the playbook and should be treated as gating: the blanket bar on assignment by Sparkling (Sections 3(c) and 20(d)) with no M&A carve-out; the mutual no-hire in Section 19 covering all employees of the other party for the term plus one year; and the complete absence of any insurance covenant even though Garman converts and processes our data and works at our Authorized Locations.

The remaining six are conventional fallback-level fixes: no aggregate liability cap or gross negligence/wilful misconduct carve-outs in Section 15; Garman's ownership of the Schedule "D" Modifications with no adequate licence back and no provision on our data; Nova Scotia governing law, which is neither our preferred nor any accepted fallback jurisdiction; the "non-transferable" licence, which cannot follow us into a merger; no services warranty and no warranty remedy in Section 12; and no post-termination transition assistance or data export anywhere in the Agreement.

---

## 2. Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant (at fallback; better than fallback on cap and exclusions) | Page 6 (§ 13) |
| 2 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | **Deviation** | § 13 Intellectual Property Indemnity (with §§ 2, 3(c), 17(a)) |
| 3 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality, carve-outs | **Deviation** | § 15 Limitation of Garman's Liability |
| 4 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | **Deviation (walk-away territory)** | Page 10 (§ 20(d); § 3(c)) |
| 5 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant (preferred) | § 2 Grant of License |
| 6 | High | LD — Liquidated damages / penalties payable by Customer | Compliant (preferred) | § 11 Fees |
| 7 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete restrictions on Customer | Compliant (preferred) | § 3 Restrictions on Use |
| 8 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Compliant (at/above fallback) | § 17 Term and Termination |
| 9 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant (above preferred; no Vendor audit right) | § 3 Restrictions on Use |
| 10 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | **Deviation** | Page 10 (§ 20(h)) |
| 11 | Medium | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | **Deviation** | § 2 Grant of License |
| 12 | Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation burdening Customer | Compliant (preferred) | § 11 Fees |
| 13 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase / volume commitments | Compliant (preferred) | § 11 Fees |
| 14 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | **Deviation (walk-away territory)** | § 19 Non-Solicitation of Employees |
| 15 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice | Compliant (preferred) | § 10 Maintenance and Support |
| 16 | Medium | TRANSITION — Exit assistance and data return | **Missing** | § 17 Term and Termination |
| 17 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | **Deviation** | § 12 Specifications and Warranty |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | **Missing (walk-away territory)** | Page 11 (§ 20 General Matters) |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

These three points fall into walk-away territory under the playbook and should be resolved before signature.

1. **Assignment (§§ 20(d) and 3(c)).** Section 20(d) is a blanket mutual bar on assignment without consent, with no successor/M&A carve-out and no reasonableness standard, and Section 3(c) separately prohibits Sparkling from assigning at all absent Garman's written authorization. A blanket prohibition on Customer assignment with no M&A carve-out is walk-away territory. We seek the fallback: successor assignment by either party on written notice, consent to other assignments not unreasonably withheld, and a conforming edit to Section 3(c).
2. **No-hire (§ 19).** Section 19 is a mutual *no-hire*, not a non-solicit: it bars each party and its affiliates from hiring any employee of the other for the term plus one year, with no general-advertising or unsolicited-approach carve-out. No-hire provisions covering all personnel are walk-away territory. We propose narrowing to a 12-month mutual non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the services, with general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs and no hiring prohibition.
3. **No insurance covenant (§ 20 General Matters).** The Agreement contains no insurance provision anywhere, yet Garman converts and processes our data under § 4(b) and performs installation, training and implementation at our Authorized Locations. That is walk-away territory. We propose the preferred package (CGL USD 1,000,000 per occurrence / USD 2,000,000 aggregate; E&O USD 2,000,000; cyber and privacy USD 5,000,000 where Garman processes any data belonging to, supplied by or processed for Sparkling; statutory workers' compensation; certificates on request), and can settle at the fallback of E&O USD 1,000,000 and cyber USD 2,000,000.

---

## 4. Next steps

**Redlines to issue with our turn of the draft:**

1. **§ 15 — liability cap.** Add a mutual 12-month fees cap plus gross negligence and wilful misconduct carve-outs. The existing "this Section 15" carve-out then automatically lifts the cap for Sections 13 and 14. We are not pursuing the preferred USD 1,000,000 floor or the additional preferred carve-outs.
2. **IP / deliverables.** Add a licence back to the Schedule "D" Modifications and Improvements (perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, including the right to modify and sublicense for our business) and confirm that any Garman licence in Sparkling's data is limited to processing solely to provide the services. Garman's ownership of its platform, tools and know-how remains intact.
3. **§§ 2, 3(c) and 20(d) — licence transferability.** Delete "non-transferable" and add a Sparkling-only successor carve-out so the licence follows us in a merger or acquisition, leaving the mutual consent requirement otherwise intact. Contractor coverage is a preferred-only point we are not pursuing.
4. **§ 20(d) / § 3(c) — assignment.** Successor assignment on written notice by either party; consent to other assignments not unreasonably withheld; conform § 3(c).
5. **§ 19 — non-solicit.** Replace the no-hire with the 12-month mutual non-solicit described above.
6. **§ 12 — warranty.** Add a 30-day services warranty covering installation, training and Maintenance Services, plus a repair/replace-or-refund remedy. The existing software conformance warranty (acceptance period plus one year from the Maintenance Commencement Date) is untouched, as it exceeds the fallback.
7. **§ 17 — exit assistance.** Insert a fallback-level provision: on expiry or termination, at least 90 days of transition assistance and export of our data within 30 days. We are not pursuing the preferred six-month/then-current-rates or certified-deletion mechanics.
8. **§ 20(h) — governing law.** Replace Nova Scotia law and non-exclusive venue with New York law and exclusive New York County state and federal courts, with a carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief. We are changing only the jurisdiction and forum words.
9. **§ 20 General Matters — insurance.** Insert the Garman insurance covenant described in Part 3.

**Diligence to close out:**

- Obtain and review Schedule "A" (Fee Schedule), which is not reproduced in the reviewed text, to confirm it contains no committed seat, location or maintenance-year minimums and no renewal uplift formula.

**Noted, not redlined:** Section 13 has no express duty to defend and no separate refund remedy if none of the (a)–(c) remedies is achievable, and the notice period is ten calendar days; given the uncapped recovery of all Losses and the Section 7/8 rejection refund, we accept the clause as drafted. Section 10 does not state that renewal requires mutual written agreement, and Section 17(b) carries no express pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; neither is a material failure."}
